resources.string: Check your hearing, create a sound profile, and listen through headphones.

EarCast is a sound-amplification and hearing-assistance tool. It is NOT a medical device and NOT a substitute for a professional hearing exam. It does not diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any condition. If you have concerns about your hearing, please see an audiologist or doctor. Always keep the volume at a comfortable level and stop if you feel any discomfort.
Amplifying sound around you. Tap Stop to turn off.
Please read and acknowledge the above before using EarCast.
No account, no ads and no internet permission. Your listening data stays on this device.
Create a profile from a guided tone check or enter an existing audiogram.

Estimate only — uncalibrated. This check is not a medical test and not a substitute for a professional hearing exam. Use headphones in a quiet room. Keep the volume comfortable; stop if anything is too loud.
You\'ll hear quiet tones at different pitches in each ear. After each tone, tap whether you heard it. It takes a couple of minutes.
Each point is the quietest level you heard at that pitch. Lower points mean quieter sounds were heard. Detailed values are listed below.
Chart of hearing check results. Detailed values are listed in the table below.
These are uncalibrated estimates, not a diagnosis. For a professional hearing assessment, see an audiologist.
Amplifies sound around you in real time. Output is hard-limited for safety, but keep the level comfortable and stop if anything is too loud. Not a medical device.
Run the hearing check first so assist mode can use your sound profile.
No headphones detected. Assist through the phone speaker usually causes loud feedback (howling). Connect earbuds or headphones — or tap Start anyway if you\'re sure.
Place the phone near a TV, speaker, or person across the table. Sound streams to your connected headphones through Hearing Assist.
Use the microphone on your connected headset while Hearing Assist processes and plays the sound back.
Stop assist before changing the microphone.
Audio could not connect. Reconnect the headset and try again.
Bluetooth microphone active: mono call audio. Detail may be limited and nearby voices may be suppressed by the earbuds. For clearer surrounding sound, try the phone microphone.

Speech clarity softens lower frequencies to bring consonants forward without extra treble volume; bass reduction softens boomy voices. Natural capture avoids extra call processing where supported. Use Call mode if Natural cannot connect.
Neural speech enhancement with optional quiet-speech boost. Runs on this device; Off noise reduction bypasses the engine.
Lightweight classic noise reduction. Try Gentle first; Strong may soften voices. Runs on this device; Off bypasses the engine.
Experimental filter for steady background noise such as fans and hiss. Adapts as you listen; changing noise or long sustained sounds may be softened. Start with Gentle and compare with Off.
DPDFNet8 is a more demanding speech model. Start with Gentle noise reduction and compare word clarity with RNNoise. Both run on this device; Off noise reduction bypasses the model.
This engine uses your fitted amplification and volume setting. The separate quiet-speech boost is available with RNNoise.
Gentle reduces background noise while keeping more surrounding sound. Strong focuses more on speech and may soften quiet voices or other sounds. Compare with Off if distant voices disappear.
Stop assist to change sound clarity settings.
Connect headphones, choose a comfortable level and start listening.
Your microphone is being shaped through your sound profile.
Gradually lifts quiet speech with noise reduction enabled. Off keeps the original speech level. Strong can also make background sound louder.
Speech profile changes apply the next time you start assist.
Profile changes apply the next time you start assist.

If you have results from a professional hearing test, enter the threshold for each pitch (in dB HL, as printed on your report). EarCast builds your sound profile from them, but does not validate the report or provide medical care.
Choose an ear, pitch and threshold above, or tap the chart. Values snap to 5 dB steps. Larger dB values appear lower on the chart.
Editable audiogram for %1$s. Tap a frequency and hearing level to set a threshold in 5 dB steps.
Play the selected point at the threshold shown above.
Uncalibrated preview. Keep the device volume comfortable and stop immediately if it is too loud.
Share a picture of your results
This image shows your estimated results. Only share it if you\'re comfortable doing so.
Estimates from an uncalibrated self-check — not a diagnosis.
Plays a short sample sound. Flip the switch to hear it shaped through your sound profile, including your amplification level. This is a simulation through your headphones, not a measurement.
If your profile has little or no adjustment, the two versions may sound similar — mostly just louder by your amplification setting.
Stop assist first — the sample can\'t play while the microphone is live.
Shows how loud assist\'s output has been, and for how long. This device isn\'t calibrated, so it\'s a relative guide — not a measurement of loudness at your ear.
Assist has been running loud for a while. Consider lowering the level or taking a break.

This check estimates how well you pick out speech from background noise. Because it compares speech against noise, your volume setting barely affects the result — just set a comfortable level first. It is an estimate, not a diagnosis, and not a substitute for a professional hearing assessment.
You\'ll hear three spoken digits mixed with noise, 24 times. After each one, type the digits you heard. The noise adapts as you go — it\'s normal for it to get hard; guess if unsure.
Type the three digits you heard.
You followed the digits down to a speech-to-noise level of about %1$d dB (estimate).
This run stayed at the edge of the check\'s range, so it can\'t give a useful number. Quiet room and headphones help — feel free to try again.
In this check, you picked out the digits even with a lot of background noise.
In this check, you picked out the digits at moderate noise levels.
In this check, background noise made the digits harder to follow. If following conversation in noisy places is a day-to-day struggle, a professional hearing assessment can tell you more.
Sets the maximum loudness assist mode will ever reach. Tap Preview, then lower the level if the tone is too loud. (For a precise dB SPL calibration you\'d need a sound-level meter — see docs.)

Balances music and videos using your sound profile. Quiet sound boost automatically backs off during loud passages to prevent buzzing. Pauses during assist, demos and hearing checks. Compatibility varies by phone.
Not supported on this device or Android version.
Run the hearing check or enter results first.
No accounts, no ads, no trackers — the app never asks for internet access, so nothing you do can leave your phone.
A little more clarity. A sound profile that feels like you. All on your phone.
Make room for the sounds you love.
Use your phone or headset microphone to listen through your headphones.
Create a personal sound profile to shape live listening, music and videos.
A personal starting point for how you listen.
Enter the values from your audiogram directly on the chart. Set each ear separately.
Listen to a few tones and answer at your own pace. The result is a rough estimate, not a medical test.
Your saved profile is ready to use.
Choose the guided check or enter an audiogram to unlock personal listening.
EarCast processes sound on your device. There are no accounts or ads. Diagnostic recording is optional, stays on your device, and is shared only when you choose Export.
EarCast is based on EarCast, licensed under GPL v3. It includes RNNoise, SpeexDSP, DPDFNet8 and sherpa-onnx. Original copyright and third-party license notices are retained with the source.
Your microphone. Your headphones. Your sound.
Choose an ear and place its points on the chart.
